directAnswer: You can find your Windows version by opening the Settings app and navigating to System > About. Alternatively, you can press Win + R, type 'winver', and press Enter.
summary: Finding your Windows version is straightforward and can be done through the Settings app or a quick command.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.body: Knowing your Windows version is essential for troubleshooting, compatibility checks, and ensuring you have the latest features and security updates.

sections.heading: Using the Settings App
sections.body: This method is applicable for Windows 10 and Windows 11 users.

sections.heading: Using the Run Command
sections.body: This method works across various Windows versions, including Windows 7, 8, 10, and 11.

steps.title: Open the Settings App
steps.detail: Click on the Start menu and select the gear icon to open Settings.

steps.title: Navigate to System
steps.detail: In the Settings window, click on 'System'.

steps.title: Select About
steps.detail: Scroll down and click on 'About' in the left sidebar to view your Windows version.

steps.title: Use the Run Command
steps.detail: Press Win + R, type 'winver', and press Enter to quickly check your Windows version.

faqs.question: What if I can't access the Settings app?
faqs.answer: You can still use the 'winver' command to find your Windows version without accessing Settings.

faqs.question: How do I know if my Windows is up to date?
faqs.answer: You can check for updates in the Settings app under Update & Security > Windows Update.

faqs.question: Can I find my Windows version on older systems?
faqs.answer: Yes, the 'winver' command works on older Windows versions like Windows 7 and 8.

caveats: The steps may vary slightly depending on your specific Windows version.
